data.title: PLTR Stock Sees Best Week In 4 Months: Palantir Bags Reported $300M Defense Deal With Poland
data.description:
Key points:
  • Poland said it would retain exclusive control over sensitive military data.
  • Palantir CEO Alex Karp announced plans to expand hiring and investment in Poland.
  • The United States reportedly used the Maven Smart System to help strike more than 1,000 targets in the first 24 hours of the Iran war.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) secured a defense contract reportedly worth around $300 million from Poland on Friday, amid an increasing use of AI in critical defense and military operations.

While the deal was announced by the Polish government, Bloomberg reported the deal’s value, citing Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz.

PLTR shares closed up 5.4%, its fifth straight session of gains and best week in nearly four months. The stock saw its best week since August, according to Koyfin data.

Poland Turns To AI For Military Decision-Making

Under a five-year agreement, Palantir will supply its artificial intelligence-powered Maven Smart System to help the Polish military analyze information, identify threats and make faster decisions.

Poland’s defense ministry said the software would operate within the military’s own infrastructure, with Palantir having no access to sensitive data, encryption keys or remote access to the system.

“All keys, servers, and information are and will remain in the exclusive possession of the Polish Army. We are purchasing the tool, but the information we will be placing and extracting from it belongs solely to Poland,” Kosiniak-Kamysz said.

The ministry added that while AI would assist in assessing threats and risks, final decisions would remain with authorized military personnel.

“We are going to begin significant investment into the Polish ecosystem, both hiring more people and looking for investment opportunities,” Palantir CEO Alex Karp said, as quoted by Bloomberg.

MSS Reportedly Helped Strike 1000 Targets With First 24 Hours In Iran War

Maven is an AI-powered platform that uses information from multiple sources, enabling the military to analyze large volumes of data through a single system. The system is also used by NATO.

The U.S. reportedly used the Maven Smart System to help strike more than 1,000 targets in the first 24 hours of the Iran war.

Retail Remains Bearish On PLTR

Despite the recent rally, retail sentiment surrounding PLTR on Stocktwits remained in ‘bearish’ territory over the past 24 hours.

PLTR shares have gained around 3% so far in 2026.

The African Export-Import Bank is due to sign a $1.45 billion financing agreement on Monday for Angola's first large-scale fertiliser plant, project developer Amufert S.A. said in a press release ahead of the ceremony.

  • The financing, together with $1.19 billion in equity already committed by shareholders, will bring total investment in the project to about $2.6 billion, the largest non-oil investment in Angola

data.title: Wall Street ends higher as battered AI stocks gain in volatile week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes up: Dow 1.18%, S&P 1.60%, Nasdaq 2.31%
  • AI-related stocks, hyperscalers gain
  • Financials post strong gains; JPMorgan up
  • All three indexes post weekly gains

By Saeed Azhar, Shashwat Chauhan and Avinash P

Wall Street's main indexes ended higher on Friday and posted weekly gains as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday and flocked to hard-hit AI-linked shares.

US stocks have swung sharply this week, with Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and Anthropic's brief fall below its initial public offering price adding to volatility across the AI trade.

Investors have alternated between bargain-hunting after a steep selloff and fretting over soaring AI costs, heavy borrowing and doubts about companies' returns on investment.

"The market is so oversold that a bounce was inevitable," said Jamie Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group.

Chipmakers that investors battered this month recovered ground, with Micron and Marvell gaining 7.6% and 7.3% respectively. The broader chip gauge also climbed 4.7%. Nvidia, after remaining weak for most of the session, ended 0.8% higher.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 591.99 points, or 1.18%, to 50,774.94, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX gained 114.71 points, or 1.60%, to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 543.70 points, or 2.31%, to 24,129.50.

AI beneficiaries, including data-storage firm Sandisk , surged almost 16%, while optical-products maker Lumentum and server maker Dell also gained sharply.

AI hyperscalers — tech companies that run large data centers — also rose, with Amazon.com , Microsoft , Meta Platforms and Oracle posting gains. Tesla surged 5%.

"There is a bounce in technology which started Monday, continued Wednesday with an intraday reversal and now continues today. So much fast money has delevered out of tech that this could have persistence next week as they are forced to chase back in," said Andrew Slimmon, senior portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

WEEKLY GAINS

For the week, the S&P 500 gained 5.6%, the Nasdaq rose 6.68%, and the Dow climbed 5.46%. The S&P 500 weekly gain was the index's biggest since April 2025.

The S&P 500 bank index (.SPXBK) rose 1.6%, fueled by JPMorgan Chase's almost 2% gain.

The market's gains have done little to erase November's losses. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq are on track for their worst November since 2008, pressured by concerns over tougher AI regulation following the Democrats' US midterm election victory and expectations that monetary policy will remain restrictive.

Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December after data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated further in October.

Gold and silver miners rallied as precious-metal prices recovered from a bruising few sessions. Newmont gained 5.4%, while the Global X Silver Miners ETF also advanced.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals slid 5.2% after the US Food and Drug Administration extended its review of the company's kidney-disease drug by up to three months.

US equity markets were open for a half-day session on Friday, following Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday.

Volume on US exchanges was 10.97 billion shares.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 3.25-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 55 new highs and 73 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 3,677 stocks rose and 1,135 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 3.24-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 12 new 52-week highs and no new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 53 new highs and 96 new lows.

data.title: Loblaw Opposes Ottawa's Canned-Vegetable Tariff, Warns of Higher Grocery Costs — Market Talk
data.description: Canadian grocer Loblaw is pushing back against Ottawa's new import tariff on canned vegetables. Loblaw says that the measures risk "raising the cost of one of the most affordable sources of nutritious food when Canadian household budgets are already under significant pressure." Loblaw, one of Canada's three dominant grocers, which recently reported a 9.7% rise in 3Q retail operating income to C$1.41 billion, adds that "Canadians should not be asked to pay more for essential food to unnecessarily shield a very large food processor from competition." Starting Dec. 1, Ottawa will impose a 50% duty on canned vegetable imports exceeding an annual 13 million kilogram quota, following a trade tribunal report that found that increased imports hurt domestic producers. Sol-Gel is a specialized dermatology company advancing innovative therapies for rare and serious skin diseases. data.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets, FT reports
data.description:
OpenAI has launched a new legal action against Apple , accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, the Financial Times reported on Friday.

The ChatGPT maker filed the lawsuit in a California court on Friday, according to the report.

Apple and OpenAI did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for talent and proprietary technology.

Earlier this year, Apple sued OpenAI and two former employees, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT owner's foray into consumer hardware. OpenAI has denied those allegations.

data.title: Vulcan seeks to overturn slim Mexico arbitration award, launches second case
data.description:
Vulcan Materials has asked an international trade tribunal to partially annul a July award that granted the US quarrying group less than 1% of the about $1.7 billion it had sought from Mexico in a long-running dispute over its operations on the country's Caribbean coast, Mexico's economy ministry said on Friday.

The compensation was granted after an arbitration tribunal under the North American Free Trade Agreement dismissed almost all of Vulcan's claims over its long-running dispute with the Mexican government over mine closures tied to environmental concerns.

Vulcan, which produces gravel and crushed stone, has denied the allegations of environmental damage. The firm did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday.

Mexico also said Vulcan had launched a second arbitration through Dutch subsidiaries under the Mexico-Netherlands investment treaty over Mexican measures taken between 2022 and 2025, which the company has said harmed its investment.

Vulcan had disclosed the new arbitration in an October financial report, saying: "We seek redress for new measures that Mexico took against us, our assets and our Mexican investments after NAFTA was no longer in force."

That dispute centers on Vulcan's limestone quarry and Punta Venado port terminal in Quintana Roo, near Playa del Carmen. Mexican authorities halted underwater quarrying in 2022, citing environmental damage, while Vulcan says the shutdowns, the suspension of its customs permit, the 2024 closure of parts of its port and a decree turning its property into a protected natural area were arbitrary and illegal.

In the document Vulcan also said it saw the July award as "negligible," and noted that "the tribunal found that Mexico violated NAFTA in several respects."

Mexico said it was reviewing Vulcan's latest claims, would mount a robust defense in both proceedings and would keep dialogue channels open with the company, while continuing to defend its sovereignty and natural resources.

The compensation granted in July amounted to about $15 million of the more than $1.7 billion sought by the US company, a government source told Reuters at the time.

data.title: Microsoft Stocks Rise 0.26% as Code Red Targets One-Hour Outage Recovery
data.description:
Microsoft shares rose 0.26% to $491.18 at 10:55 a.m. ET on Friday, November 27, in the shortened regular session, as investors weighed an internal Code Red push to fix Microsoft 365 reliability. Memos reviewed by Reuters show the company wants to resolve future global incidents within an hour, a goal Microsoft 365 Core president Jason Henderson acknowledged it does not yet meet.

The trigger was a nearly 24-hour outage on November 12 and 13 that knocked out Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams and Copilot. Microsoft's preliminary review traced it to a July fix for networking gateway servers and lock contention in an internal Windows process, leaving more than 80% of servers unresponsive at the worst point. Outage reports peaked at about 130,000 across 74 countries, TweakTown reported, and Satya Nadella apologized.

The GuruFocus chart shows a perfect GF Score of 100/100, with elite profitability, a strong balance sheet and top-tier momentum. The GF Value of $606.32 implies a 19.0% discount, which GuruFocus rates modestly undervalued, so the market is not treating the outage as lasting damage. The commercial risk is real, though: Copilot is sold on top of Microsoft 365, and every hour of downtime weakens the case for charging enterprises more per seat. The next test is Microsoft's final post-incident report and whether commercial bookings hold up next quarter.

data.title: U.S. Stocks Move Sharply Higher, Post Substantial Weekly Gains
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - With trading resuming following the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday, stocks moved sharply higher over the course of the trading session on Friday. The major averages all showed strong moves to the upside after closing mixed for two straight days.

The major averages ended the day just off their highs of the session. The Nasdaq surged 543.70 points or 2.3 percent to 24,129.50, the S&P 500 shot up 114.71 points or 1.6 percent to 7,297.49 and the Dow jumped 591.99 points or 1.2 percent to 50,774.94.

For the holiday-interrupted week, the Nasdaq soared by 6.7 percent, while the S&P 500 and the Dow both spiked by around 5 and a half percent.

The rally on Wall Street reflected an extension of the substantial volatility seen over the past few sessions.

Stocks have shown wild swings in recent days amid shifting views about the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade due in part to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and subsequent reinstatement.

Tech stocks extended the recovery from an early sell-off on Wednesday, as reflected by the surge by the tech-heavy Nasdaq.

'Investors will be counting their blessings that the pre-Thanksgiving recovery in global tech stocks looks like it's being sustained after the turkey has been cleared from people's plates,' says AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould.

He added, 'After a tumultuous week, there will be hopes this uptick can be sustained and that the momentum can carry over into the remainder of the year, despite worries about the sustainability of AI spending, rising borrowing costs and a renewed tariff threat.'

However, overall trading activity was somewhat subdued amid a lack of major U.S. economic data and an early close on Wall Street.

Sector News

Gold stocks skyrocketed amid a sharp increase by the price of the precious metal, with the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index soaring by 6.9 percent.

Substantial strength was also visible among computer hardware stocks, as reflected by the 5.6 percent spike by the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index.

Semiconductor and networking stocks also saw considerable strength, contributing to the jump by the tech-heavy Nasdaq.

Energy stocks also turned in a strong performance despite a downturn by the price of crude oil, while airline, retail and financial stocks also moved notably higher.

Other Markets

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved sharply higher during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index jumped by 2.1 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index surged by 3.7 percent.

The major European markets also moved to the upside on the day. While the French CAC 40 Index rose by 0.6 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index climbed by 0.8 percent and the German DAX Index advanced by 0.9 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries have shown a significant pullback following recent strength. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has shot up 9.2 basis points to 4.940 percent.

data.title: M&A lift: Home Depot and Lowe's are hammering out post-deal synergies
data.description:
Home improvement giants Home Depot and Lowe's updated investors and analysts during their recent earnings conference calls on how their biggest acquisitions are helping them win more business from professional contractors.

Home Depot bought SRS Distribution, which serves roofers, landscapers, and pool contractors, for $18.3B in 2024. SRS has since added GMS and the HVAC distributor Mingledorff's. It now runs five business lines from more than 1.3K locations. SRS's third-quarter sales rose 25.1% to $4.87 billion, helped by those acquisitions. Its mix is also more balanced. Roofing fell to about 38% of SRS sales from 50% a year earlier, so the business depends less on storm-driven demand, which may appeal to investors.

Looking ahead, Home Depot's biggest opportunity may be selling more of its products to SRS customers. "We're on track to meet the $400 million goal that we laid out for 2026, and we look to double that in 2027," highlighted Mike Rowe, Home Depot's executive vice president of Pro. Customers that used to buy in one category are now buying across several. Home Depot plans to open 40 to 50 new SRS branches this year.

Meanwhile, Lowe's responded to Home Depot's aggressive M&A moves with an agreement to buy Foundation Building Materials, a distributor of interior building products, for approximately $8.8B. That deal is already producing savings, according to CFO Brandon Sink, who noted the purchasing benefits in drywall, steel, and insulation were largely realized in 2026 and will carry into 2027. Plans to increase sales are still being tested, which leaves room for more gains. They include selling Lowe's products to FBM customers and letting those customers use their FBM credit in Lowe's stores. Sink noted excess cash can pay for most of FBM's 15 planned new branches and small acquisitions, while paying down debt stays a priority for the company. Lowe's will give more detail on FBM at an investor conference on December 9.

data.title: SMX Gains on Newspaper Article
data.description:
SMX (NYSE:SMX) shares gained Friday, as the company, a pioneer in molecular marking and digital material authentication technology, was featured this week in an opinion piece published by The Denver Post examining the need for greater transparency, traceability and accountability in Colorado's evolving recycling economy.

The article, titled "Colorado Has Built a Recycling Framework. Now It Needs Proof," was published on November 23 and addresses one of the most pressing challenges facing states as they implement ambitious environmental legislation: establishing credible proof that materials are being recycled and returned to the economy.

Colorado has made significant strides in advancing sustainability through its Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) legislation, which places greater accountability on manufacturers and producers for the lifecycle of packaging materials. The next opportunity lies in establishing the technological infrastructure to support those policies.

SMX's proprietary molecular marking technology and Digital Material Passport Platform (DMPP) are designed to address this challenge by giving physical materials a persistent identity linked to a secure digital record.

The technology enables businesses to authenticate materials, establish chain of custody, document recycled content and create audit-ready records throughout the supply chain.

SMX shares charged 16 cents, or 7.8%, to $2.20.

data.title: European Markets Finish Higher, Extend Thursday's Gains
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - The major European markets found additional support on Friday, extending gains from the previous session thanks to easing concerns over the outlook for artificial intelligence stocks.

The markets opened higher and remained in the green throughout the trading day, ending near session highs on strength from the technology stocks and mining companies. Copper and gold prices recovered, helping spur a rally in the mining sector, while AI-driven market jitters eased after authorities in South Korea and China announced support measures.

The DAX in Germany climbed 225.72 points or 0.90 percent to finish at 25,441.24, while the FTSE in London gained 89.51 points or 0.84 percent to close at 10.698.81, the CAC 40 in France added 47.35 points or 0.58 percent to end at 8,156.09 and the SMI in Switzerland collected 62.29 points or 0.42 percent to finish at 14,879.97.

In economic news, Finland's economy grew less than estimated in the third quarter, Statistics Finland said on Friday. Gross domestic product advanced a seasonally and working-day-adjusted 0.3 percent sequentially in the third quarter, after rising 0.2 percent in the previous quarter. In the flash estimate, the expansion was 0.5 percent.

Sweden's economic growth moderated less than estimated in the third quarter, Statistics Sweden said on Friday. Gross domestic product rose 0.5 percent sequentially in the third quarter, slower than the revised 1.4 percent rebound in the second quarter. In the flash estimate, the rate of increase was 0.4 percent.

The French economy contracted more than estimated in the third quarter, revised data from the statistical office INSEE showed Friday. Gross domestic product shrank 0.2 percent after remaining flat in the preceding period. The decline for the third quarter was revised down from -0.1 percent.

Spain's consumer price inflation eased more than expected in November to the lowest level in four months, flash data from the statistical office INE revealed Friday. The consumer price index climbed 4.1 percent annually in November, slower than October's stable increase of 4.9 percent. Economists had expected inflation to moderate to 4.6 percent. Core inflation also eased to 2.6 percent from 3.1 percent in October.

data.title: SunPower Receives Notice of Deficiency from Nasdaq Related to Delayed Filing of Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for Third Quarter 2026
data.description:
OREM, Utah, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SunPower Inc. (Nasdaq “SPWR”) today announced that it received a deficiency notification letter from the Listing Qualifications staff of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) on November 23, 2026 (the "Notice"). The Notice indicated that the Company was not in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) (the “Listing Rule”) because it did not timely file its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 27, 2026 (the “Q3 Form 10-Q”). The Listing Rules require Nasdaq-listed companies to timely file all required periodic reports with the SEC. The Notice has no immediate effect on the listing of the Company’s common stock or warrants.

In accordance with Nasdaq’s listing rules, the Company has 60 calendar days after the Notice to submit a plan to regain compliance with the Listing Rule. The Company continues to work diligently to complete its Q3 Form 10-Q. The Company intends to file its Q3 Form 10-Q as promptly as possible to retain compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1).

data.title: CryptoQuant says bitcoin price recovery needs USDT supply growth
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC) needs USDT supply to start growing again for a sustained price recovery, according to CryptoQuant. The stablecoin's supply across Ethereum and Tron has seen its biggest 60-day decline since August 2022.

USDT supply across the two blockchains fell by $8.1 billion, or 4.4%, in the 60 days through Nov. 23, CryptoQuant said in a Thursday report. The combined supply stood at $174.5 billion, down $12.9 billion from its record high in May.

Almost all of the 60-day decline came from Ethereum. USDT supply on Tron remained largely unchanged. Earlier this year, growth in USDT supply on Tron helped offset the decline on Ethereum, but that is no longer the case.

Between Oct. 9 and Nov. 23, holders sent $11.65 billion worth of USDT back to Tether's treasury on Ethereum, compared with $4.19 billion sent out by the treasury. Tether also burned $8 billion worth of USDT in two batches. USDT supply on Ethereum fell to $80.3 billion, its lowest level since August 2025, CryptoQuant said.

Two crypto exchanges, Bitfinex and Binance, accounted for 89% of the USDT sent back to Tether's treasury on Ethereum. However, CryptoQuant found that about $2.8 billion of the USDT sent by Binance was matched by the issuance of the same amount on Tron within two hours. This suggests Binance was moving some of its USDT from Ethereum to Tron rather than reducing its USDT holdings.

What CryptoQuant is watching

"Bitcoin has not made a new high while USDT supply was contracting, and its 60-day returns have been negative most of the time when liquidity was leaving," CryptoQuant wrote.

The firm found that bitcoin had closed at record highs 39 times since 2022, and none of those came during periods when USDT supply was falling.

Bitcoin's price fell by an average of 9.5% over 60-day periods when USDT supply was shrinking. In comparison, bitcoin gained an average of 7.6% when USDT supply was growing.

"A recovery in liquidity is a necessary condition for a sustainable price recovery," CryptoQuant said.

The firm is now watching for three things: USDT supply to start growing again on a 60-day basis, the decline in USDT supply on Ethereum to stop, and the amount of USDT going out of Tether's treasury to exceed the amount coming back in.
